Daniel Huffmann has written an [interesting blog post][article] shedding light on how he uses (or
has tried to use) generative AI[^genai] for cartography projects. The [post][article] opens with
Daniel stating his generally critical stance towards AI and its extractive nature. He goes on:

> Despite all this, I find myself using genAI^[Generative AI.] from time to time. Is this 
hypocritical? Quite possibly. But, it’s also not far off from human nature. It’s hard for many of us 
to resist the temptation to see what this interesting new tool can do.

[![Georeferencing a raster map using Claude (source: Daniel Huffmann)](georeferencing.png "Georeferencing a raster map using Claude (source: Daniel Huffmann)")][article]

The rest of the [article][article] highlights some genAI uses Daniel has applied in his work. Some
of these I consider quite creative and hadn't occurred to me before. I also appreciate that
Daniel is upfront when a test hasn't worked out well:

> None of what I present above is definitive, or a proper study. Just a handful of anecdotes, 
including of some subpar results. But, I think all of these examples point towards ways that genAI 
might make its way into some cartographic pipelines. [...] For the cartographers that are excited to 
use these tools, I wanted to suggest constructive, practical directions. Importantly, my suggested 
genAI uses (1) don’t significantly undercut the human creative aspect, (2) can easily be checked for 
errors, and (3) might actually save time and labor (if not now, probably soon).

Overall, a clear-eyed and [interesting perspective and source of inspiration][article].

[article]: https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/2026/09/08/genai-for-the-static-cartographer/

[^genai]: Artificial intelligence systems that generate new media (text, code, images, audio, video) rather than only analysing or classifying existing data.
